sentences.text:
THE HONOURABLE SRI JUSTICE K.SURENDER  CRIMINAL APPEAL No.1564 OF 2010 JUDGMENT:
1. The appellant was convicted for the offence under Section 376 of IPC and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for seven years.
2. The prosecution filed charge sheet against this appellant as A-1 and two others The charges leveled against the accused are under Sections 376, 417, 420 and 109 of IPC.
3. P.W.1 is the victim.
The acquitted accused A-2 and A-3 are the parents of the accused/A-1.
According to P.W.1, she was in love with the appellant for two years and stayed in their house on the promise that the appellant would marry her.
She stayed for a period of three months and they had sexual intercourse during that period.
After three months, she was sent away.
Since the acquitted accused A-2 and A-3 were also aware about the relationship between the victim/P.W.1 and the appellant, they were arrayed as accused.
However, learned Assistant Sessions Judge acquitted A-2 and A-3 of all the charges.
4. The basis of conviction under Section 376 of IPC is the statement made by P.W.1 that they had sexual intercourse for a period three months.
5. During the course of cross-examination, P.W.1 admitted that she belongs to koya community and she entered into the house of the accused on her own accord.
One type of marriage was to pay 'Alavakattamamullu' which would involve payment of money to the elders for protection.
She also admitted that money was paid by A-2 and A-3 to the elders.
6. Even according to her statement she had voluntarily lived with the appellant as husband and wife after concluding the customary ceremony of marriage.

In the said circumstances, when there is no allegation of any forcible intercourse or that the victim was staying with the appellant under a wrong impression of being married, none of the ingredients of Section 376 of IPC are made out.
For the said reason, conviction under Section 376 of IPC is hereby set aside.
7. Accordingly, the Criminal Appeal is allowed.
The bail bonds shall stand cancelled.
Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
